t: Here on the south side of Oxford Street once stood the Pantheon, a place of public entertainment. It opened in 1772, designed by James Wyatt. Its main rotunda was one of the largest rooms built in England up to that time, with a dome that recalled the Pantheon in Rome. It began as winter assembly rooms and was briefly a theatre. Later it was a bazaar and a wine merchant's showroom, until demolition in 1937. Today a Marks and Spencer branch occupies the site.
